articles.title: Coco Gauff draws on Tiafoe and ‘delusional’ self-belief in US Open escape
articles.summary: American rallies from brink to defeat Andreeva. Gauff survives 12 double faults in three-set escape. Coco Gauff has played far cleaner matches than on Wednesday afternoon.
body: The 22-year-old American’s serene march through the US Open women’s draw hit extreme turbulence early in her quarter-final clash with fifth-seeded Mirra Andreeva inside Arthur Ashe Stadium. She dropped the first four games before surrendering the opening set in 26 minutes, ending a streak of 20 consecutive sets won dating back nearly a month. She piled up 12 double faults and 42 unforced errors, the majority off a forehand in open revolt. She found herself one point from defeat not once but twice during a hairy second-set tiebreaker.

But the fourth-seeded Gauff somehow wriggled free, prevailing 2-6, 7-6 (7), 6-2 over the reigning French Open champion to extend a 10-match winning streak and reach the last four in New York for the first time since her grand slam breakthrough three years ago.
“Yeah, I mean, it was a slow start,” Gauff said. “I thought Mirra was playing a great level to come out, wasn’t really making a lot of mistakes, and forcing me into some errors.
“I think I was also, like, giving away points too sometimes or trying to end the point early, because I felt the pressure from her. I was able to reset and somehow get out of that one.”

articles.title: Champions League roundup: Raphinha shines as Barcelona thrash Feyenoord
articles.summary: Brazilian scores twice in 5-1 victory at Camp Nou. Torres scores hat-trick as PSG thump Slovan Bratislava. Raphinha let his goals do the talking after being omitted from the Ballon d’Or shortlist, striking twice as Barcelona eased to a 5-1 win over Feyenoord in the Champions League.
body: The Brazilian was a surprise omission from this week’s 30-strong list of candidates for the prestigious award but brushed any disappointment aside to continue his early season hot streak at a rain-soaked Camp Nou. The forward finished brilliantly in the third minute and added a second just before the hour mark to down the Eredivisie side and take his tally to eight goals in six outings at the start of the campaign.

The summer signing Karim Adeyemi produced a stunning finish, Lamine Yamal stroked a free-kick through a gap in the Dutch wall and recent arrival Gabriel Jesus opened his account for the club just two minutes after stepping off the bench.
There was little to celebrate for Giovanni van Bronckhorst on his Barça return but Sem Steijn gave the visiting fans something to enjoy when he poked in at far post late on.

“The most important thing is we are playing like a team, like one unit,” the Barcelona head coach, Hansi Flick, said. “We controlled the game, we are dominant and this is fantastic to see. This is our style and how we want to play.”

articles.title: Star subs rescue Chelsea as Alonso 'takes blame'
articles.summary: Chelsea get the better of Leeds in a cup thriller, but Blues boss Xabi Alonso has food for thought after needing rescue act from his star substitutes.
body: Xabi Alonso watched his Chelsea team hit six goals in the second half against Leeds United but felt the need to "take responsibility" for the shaky start that came before the thrilling flurry.

Amid jubilation that followed the final whistle at Stamford Bridge, where Chelsea recovered from 2-0 down to progress as 6-3 winners in the Carabao Cup, it was easy to forget that Alonso's side were booed off at half-time.
Supporters witnessed arguably the worst first half of Alonso's short tenure to date, with Chelsea fortunate not to be further in arrears after the head coach made nine changes to his line-up.
The team's rhythm was disrupted. Leeds made eight changes themselves, but Daniel Farke's side took control and were threatening to surge into the fourth round.

articles.title: Rybakina sinks Zheng to grab No 1 spot and set up US Open semi-final with Gauff
articles.summary: Rybakina into semis after 3-6, 6-1, 6-4 victory. Coco Gauff battles back to beat Mirra Andreeva. Elena Rybakina will become the No 1 woman in the world for the first time after orchestrating a supreme recovery to reach the semi-finals of the US Open with a 3-6, 6-1, 6-4 win over the Olympic…
body: By becoming just the 30th player in the history of the WTA to reach the No 1 ranking, Rybakina ends Aryna Sabalenka’s extended spell at the top. The Belarusian has held the position for 99 successive weeks, the sixth-longest consecutive reign in history, and 107 weeks in total.

During last year’s North American hardcourt swing, Rybakina fell out of the top 10 and she was struggling badly with her health and game. She has responded with by far the best year of her career, following up her WTA Finals triumph in November with her second grand slam title at the Australian Open, four years after her first triumph at Wimbledon. She has also won titles in Ningbo and Stuttgart in addition to finishing runner-up in Indian Wells and Toronto.

Between Sabalenka’s difficult past five months and Rybakina’s resurgence, the Kazakhstani arrived in New York fully conscious of the opportunity before her. The No 1 ranking was always in her hands, with a run to the semi-final guaranteeing it from the beginning.

articles.title: Scottish roundup: Miovski hits last-gasp Rangers winner and Celtic keep 100% record
articles.summary: Rangers beat St Mirren 1-0 at Ibrox. Celtic also narrow winners at St Johnstone. A dramatic last-gasp strike from substitute Bojan Miovski gave Rangers a 1-0 Premiership win over St Mirren at Ibrox.
body: Back in the technical area after a two-game touchline suspension, Derek McInnes watched St Mirren’s Australian goalkeeper Jacob Chapman keep the home side at bay in the first half with a string of saves, albeit helped by some poor finishing.

Craig McLeish’s side, who lost 5-1 at Ibrox in the Premier Sports Cup last month, grew in confidence after the break and Fraser Taylor missed a great chance while the frustrated home support returned to the state of agitation which characterised the start of the season.
However, in the final seconds of normal time, Miovski, on for Djeidi Gassama, pounced in the box to grab the winner to make it four victories in a row.
Summer signing Mika Baur notched his first goal for Celtic as the Scottish champions maintained their perfect start to their title defence with a 1-0 victory away to St Johnstone.

articles.title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit
articles.summary: Prince William urges sport at every level to make suicide prevention part of its culture through a new nationwide toolkit called On Your Side.
body: Prince William has urged sport at every level to make suicide prevention part of its culture through a new nationwide toolkit.

Launched by the Prince of Wales and the Royal Foundation, On Your Side, external is a set of resources available online that aims "to make suicide prevention as much a part of sport as warm-up, training and performance".
The project is backed by more than 70 organisations including the Football Association, Premier League, Team GB, British Cycling and a host of leading mental health charities.

"Through my work on mental health, I have met people whose lives have been changed forever by suicide," said Prince William. "But I have also met people whose lives have been saved because someone stepped in to help."

articles.title: BMW Signs Brad Binder To Factory WSBK Team
articles.summary: Binder reunites with Oliveira. Brad Binder's next chapter starts on a production-based bike. BMW confirmed the South African will join its factory ROKiT BMW Motorrad WorldSBK Team for 2027. Binder had been a fixture of the Grand Prix paddock since 2012.
body: Binder will line up alongside Miguel Oliveira, whose deal to stay with BMW for 2027 was confirmed last week, ahead of the French round at Magny-Cours. The pairing reunites two riders who already know each other's habits intimately, having shared a garage across Moto3, Moto2 and MotoGP during their KTM years. The two remain the only riders to have ever won a MotoGP race on a KTM.

With two riders signed for next season, Danilo Petrucci's run in the BMW WorldSBK project will end after the 2026 season. BMW says it is exploring ways to keep the Italian involved elsewhere. "At the same time, we would like to thank Danilo for his tremendous commitment," said Sven Blusch, head of BMW Motorrad Motorsport. "Together, we want to finish the current season strongly and are working towards a future together in other projects."

articles.title: Barry Melrose, Entertaining ESPN Hockey Analyst, Dies at 70
articles.summary: After 11 pro seasons as a rugged player, he led the L.A. Kings to the Stanley Cup Final in his first season as an NHL coach, then handled colorful commentary from 1994-2022.
body: Barry Melrose, the blue-collar NHL defenseman who brought flash to the Los Angeles Kings as their coach and fun to ESPN during his nearly three decades as a colorful hockey analyst, has died. He was 70.

National Hockey League Commissioner Gary Bettman confirmed Melrose’s death in a statement shared with The Hollywood Reporter. “From the flowing locks of his distinctive mullet to the flared lapels of his trademark long suit coats, Barry Melrose cut an unmistakable figure whenever you were fortunate enough to run into him at a rink or catch him on your television screen. You were even more fortunate if you engaged him in conversation or listened to his analysis, because he never failed to boost your love of the game of hockey,” he wrote.

“A rangy and rugged defenseman from Kelvington, Saskatchewan, Barry fashioned an 11-year pro career in the NHL, AHL and WHA. But it was as a coach, who guided the Los Angeles Kings to the 1993 Stanley Cup Final, and as a broadcaster, who spent 27 years at ESPN, that he truly made his mark upon the game. And during those countless encounters over the years with players, coaches, fans and viewers who couldn’t help but be drawn in by his enthusiasm.

articles.title: Top four in the world set for US Open women's semi-final showdown
articles.summary: Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka will bid to move one step closer to a third straight US Open title when she faces familiar foe ‌Jessica Pegula, while Elena Rybakina will take on home favourite Coco Gauff in the semi-finals on Thursday from midnight - live on Sky Sports Tennis.
body: For the first time since Wimbledon in ​2009, all four top seeds at a Grand Slam have reached the semi-finals, with Sabalenka, Rybakina and Gauff all former major champions and third seed Pegula seeking a maiden Grand Slam title.

Sabalenka has reached the semi-finals here for a sixth consecutive year and is now two wins away from becoming the first woman ‌since Serena Williams from 2012 to 2014 to win three straight titles in New York.
The top seed had not dropped a set before surviving her toughest test of the tournament ​on Tuesday, edging Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova.

The Belarusian will face a familiar opponent in third seed Pegula, with their rivalry returning to Flushing Meadows for a third straight year after Sabalenka denied the American the title in 2024 and then beat her ​again in last year's semi-finals.

articles.title: Arteta explains new role for transformed Odegaard
articles.summary: Martin Odegaard is a player transformed at the start of this season - and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta puts his captain's impressive form down to fitness and new positioning.
body: Odegaard was the match-winner again for Arsenal on Wednesday, thumping in the only goal of the game in the Champions League victory at Napoli.
That hit followed his clinching strike against Chelsea in the Premier League on Sunday and takes his total to four goals in five appearances this season across all competitions.
Odegaard only scored once for Arsenal during an injury-hit 2025/26 campaign but now his stats are up across a range of other attacking metrics, too.
"First of all he needs to be available and last year he missed so many games through injuries," said Arteta when asked in his post-match press conference about Odegaard's improvement.

articles.title: Chelsea hit SIX second-half goals to see off Leeds in Carabao Cup classic
articles.summary: An incredible second-half comeback including six goals in 41 minutes saw Chelsea finally blow away Leeds 6-3 in one of the all-time Carabao Cup classics at Stamford Bridge.
body: The Blues found themselves two goals behind when Brenden Aaronson struck after 47 minutes to add to Tarik Muharemovic's opener, and it appeared Xabi Alonso's first real cup test would end in disappointment - despite the half-time introduction of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers, Pedro Neto and Reece James.
A Palmer penalty turned the game on its head suddenly after Pep Chavarria was caught by Dan James, but it was Rogers who inspired the comeback, making four of Chelsea's six goals.

Three of those assists - for Palmer's second, Neto's strike and the first of two for Danny Welbeck - came as Chelsea netted three times more in 12 minutes, including Welbeck's fourth which should have given them breathing space when he fired through Michael Zetterer's legs.

Not for the first time in Alonso's short reign however, chaos once again reigned over control as Leeds continued to create chances before Dominic Calvert-Lewin pulled them back to within a goal with 15 minutes to go.
